Finally, we proceed to the main result of this section. We show that if G is a nontrivial
(k, g, s)-multipole with s ≤(k −2)g, then it cannot happen that |G| ≤b1(k, g, s). Thus, we
obtain a nontrivial lower bound on the size of G.

By Lemma 3 we also assume that G contains no vertex with inner degree 1.

|G′| ≥b2(k, g, (k −2)g)) and then |G| ≥b2(k, g, (k −2)g) + 1. Thus, k = 3.
